title: What is the difference between stored procedures and functions in SQL Server?
description: Understand when to use stored procedures versus functions.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between stored procedures and functions in SQL Server?

Stored procedures are precompiled SQL statements that can perform operations and return results. Functions are routines that return a single value and can be used in SQL statements. Functions must return a value; stored procedures can return zero or multiple values.

**Stored Procedures:**
- Can perform DML operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)
- Can return multiple result sets
- Can have input and output parameters
- Can call functions
- Used for business logic
- Executed with EXECUTE command
- Can have side effects

**Functions:**
- Must return a value (scalar or table)
- Can be used in SELECT statements
- Can only have input parameters
- Cannot modify database state (mostly)
- Used for computations
- Called from SQL statements
- No side effects

**Key Differences:**
- Functions return values, procedures don't have to
- Functions can be used in queries, procedures can't
- Procedures can modify data, functions shouldn't
- Functions support table-valued returns
- Procedures support error handling (TRY-CATCH)
